_why: The master has no timeout on `gh pr list` at all; a hung `gh` stalls the .ps1 side for tests/parity.py's own OLD_SIDE_TIMEOUT (45s), which parity.py records as the sentinel 'TIMEOUT'. The new side is bounded by thresholds.subprocess_timeout_remote_sec (20s) and fails open (ALLOW) plus logs to dispatch-errors.jsonl -- it never silently skips a slow-but-eventually-successful gh call, it just cannot wait indefinitely. This fixture exercises the new-side timeout path directly via a stubbed ctx.run_cmd that reports timed_out=True; the parity-side TIMEOUT sentinel comparison is tests/parity.py's responsibility once the old side is run for real.
